q: The Host-Kra seminorms ||f||_{U^k} (Gowers-Host-Kra norms in ergodic theory) are defined by the recurrence ||f||_{U^{k+1}}^{2^{k+1}} = lim_{N→∞} (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ||f · T^n f||_{U^k}^{2^k}. These seminorms control the convergence of multiple ergodic averages because:
opts: ||f||_{U^2} = 0 if and only if f is 'anti-correlated' with all degree-1 polynomial phases — any f with ||f||_{U^{k+1}} = 0 is orthogonal to all (k+1)-step nilsystems
They measure the L² norm of f
exp: Host-Kra: f has ||f||_{U^{k+1}} = 0 iff f is orthogonal (in L²) to all (k+1)-step nilsystems. The characteristic factor for k-term arithmetic progression averages is the (k-1)-step nilfactor (generated by nilsystems). These seminorms are the ergodic-theoretic analogues of Gowers norms in combinatorics.
